title: RequestLog
description:
A record of a proxied API request.

On `GET /logs` the fields `id`, `request_id`, `tenant_id`, `route_id`,
`matched_client_id`, `identification_method`, `method`, `status_code`,
`src_ip`, `environment`, `sandbox` and `ts` are exactly what the Merkle
anchor commits to, in that order - see `GET /logs/{request_id}/proof`.
Every other field is operational detail and is NOT part of the leaf.

id.description: Row id as a decimal string. This is `api_requests.id`, a bigint - NOT a uuid, which earlier revisions of this schema incorrectly declared. It is a string rather than a JSON number because a JSON number is a double and cannot hold a bigint exactly past 2^53.

request_id.description: Correlation ID for the proxied request.

src_ip.description: Source IP address of the caller, host form without a prefix length. Identity tier on `GET /logs`: requires `log:read_identity`, and is ABSENT (not null) when denied.

status_code.description: HTTP status code returned by the upstream.

upstream_host.description: Upstream host the request was forwarded to.

error.description: Error message if the request failed.

environment.description: Environment the request was resolved against.

signature_valid.description: Whether the request signature was valid (if required).

source_ip_country.description: Country of the source IP (GeoIP lookup).

source_ip_city.description: City of the source IP (GeoIP lookup).

tenant_id.description: Owning tenant. Returned by `GET /logs`; omitted by `GET /routes/{id}/logs`.

matched_client_id.description: Which client the request was attributed to. Kept when that client is later deleted, so it may name a client that no longer exists: it is a committed field of the row's Merkle leaf and is never rewritten. Identity tier on `GET /logs`: requires `log:read_identity`, and is ABSENT (not null) when denied.

identification_method.description: How that attribution was made (e.g. `ip`, `mtls_thumbprint`). Identity tier on `GET /logs`.

sandbox.description: Live/Test partition. `null` on rows written before the partition existed, which are treated as Live. Null, false and true are three distinct facts and the Merkle anchor keeps them apart.

cursor.description: Opaque resume token, returned by `GET /logs` only. Pass the last row's value as `cursor` on the next call.

client_origin.description: How the call arrived at the Route. `sdk_intercept`: a KnoxCall SDK's route-aware interceptor rerouted a third-party SDK's request onto the Route (the SDK sent `x-knoxcall-origin: sdk-intercept`). `direct`: a plain `call()` / bound-route request, and every row written before the marker existed. Informational only - it never influences authentication, routing, rate limits or the response block.
